narrative.overview:
Brainagram is a technical drawing that keeps time. Everything at rest is calm and neutral — paper and graphite in the light theme, graphite and chalk in the dark — so that the one thing that matters stands out: the **impulse**, the violet dot that travels along the active arrow and lights up what is happening *now*. The past stays in quiet ink (done), the future in thin, legible grey (pending), and the present glows (active). Every visual decision serves that reading of time.

The interface is an instrument, not a stage: dense, precise and quiet, with short shadows, 1px hairlines and small, exact type. Personality lives in the details — named motion curves, node shapes that carry meaning, a scrubber segmented by step — rather than in decoration. There is no neon, no gradient, no "dark hacker" look; the dark theme is graphite tinted toward violet, not an inverted light theme.

The same tokens drive the application chrome and the SVG diagram, and the SVG export inlines the active theme's values, so a diagram looks the same in the app, in a PNG and in a GIF.
keyCharacteristics: One saturated color, reserved for motion, the current step, the primary action and focus.
Technical-drawing neutrals: warm paper (light), violet-tinted graphite (dark).
Meaning carried by form first — line style, arrowhead, node shape — and color second.
Compact 4px rhythm, 32px controls, 1px borders, short shadows.
Named motion curves for the impulse, the arrival pulse and reveals; reduced motion fully supported.
Plain hand-written CSS on custom properties; both themes share every token name.

rules.name: The One Live Signal Rule
rules.body: Violet means "moving or happening now". If something violet neither moves nor responds to an action, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Form Before Color Rule
rules.body: Arrow kinds are read by line style and arrowhead, node kinds by shape and glyph; color only reinforces.

rules.name: The Token-Only Rule
rules.body: Components never use literal colors. Both themes swap the same names; anything drawn in the canvas uses a `--` token listed in the export (`EXPORT_VARS`).

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Time, zoom, counters and step numbers use Geist Mono with `tabular-nums`, so playing never makes digits jitter.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Everything is sentence case except overlines, which are uppercase.

rules.name: The Float-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "this sits above the canvas or the page". Cards and panels at rest are bordered, not lifted; a card may lift 2px on hover.

rules.name: The Participant Row Rule
rules.body: On the landing, navigation is the diagram's participant row: one header per section, each sitting on its own lifeline, the last one the filled demo action. Don't add a separate nav bar, menu or tab strip beside it.

rules.name: The Step Wash Rule
rules.body: `--step-wash` exists only in `site/` and only as the full-bleed band behind the current step's heading. Everywhere else the selection ground is `brand-soft`.

dos: **Do** reserve `brand` for what moves or is current: the impulse, the active arrow, the current step, one primary action, focus.
**Do** use tokens for every color, in the app and in the canvas, and add any new canvas token to `EXPORT_VARS`.
**Do** distinguish kinds and states by form (line style, arrowhead, node shape, icon + word) before color.
**Do** keep text at 4.5:1 and control edges, arrows, icons and focus at 3:1 in both themes.
**Do** dim inactive diagram elements by swapping tokens (e.g. `text-muted`, `border`), not by lowering opacity on text.
**Do** use Geist Mono with tabular numbers for time, zoom, counters and code.
**Do** keep controls at 32px on the 4px rhythm, with 1px hairlines and the shadow vocabulary above.
donts: **Don't** paint anything violet that neither moves nor responds to an action.
**Don't** use neon, gradients or a "dark hacker" look; the dark theme is graphite, not black.
**Don't** fill whole nodes with their kind color — only the glyph and its tile.
**Don't** use Unicode glyphs or emoji as icons; use Heroicons through `<.icon>`, with an `aria-label` that names the shortcut on icon-only buttons.
**Don't** introduce a CSS framework, utility classes or literal hex values in components.
**Don't** lift cards and panels at rest with shadows; shadows are for what floats.
